questions.q: If f(1) = 1, f'(1) = 3 then the derivative of f(f(f(x))) + (f(x))$^2$ at x = 1 is
questions.explanation: By chain rule, d/dx[f(f(f(x)))] at x=1 = f'(1)·f'(1)·f'(1) = 27 (since f(1)=1 repeatedly). d/dx[(f(x))^2] at x=1 = 2f(1)f'(1) = 6. Total = 27+6 = 33.

questions.q: If y = x$^{\sin x}$ + (\sin x)$^x$ then dy/dx at x = $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: Using logarithmic differentiation, at x=π/2: derivative of x^{sinx} works out to 1, and derivative of (sinx)^x works out to 0, giving dy/dx = 1.

questions.q: If y = e$^{\sqrt{x\sqrt{x\sqrt{x\cdots}}}}$, x > 1 then $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at x = log$_e$3 is
questions.explanation: Let L = \sqrt{xL} (infinite nested radical), giving L=x, so y=e^x and y''=e^x. At x=\ln 3, y''=e^{\ln 3}=3.

If e$^y$ + xy = e the ordered pair $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}, \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)$ at x = 0 is equal to
questions.explanation: At x=0, y=1. Implicit differentiation gives y' = -y/(e^y+x) = -1/e, and differentiating again gives y'' = 1/e^2.

questions.q: The function f(x) = log(1 + x) - $\dfrac{2x}{2+x}$ is increasing on
questions.explanation: $f'(x) = \frac{1}{1+x} - \frac{4}{(2+x)^2} = \frac{x^2}{(1+x)(2+x)^2} \ge 0$ whenever $x>-1$, so f is increasing on $(-1,\infty)$.

questions.q: The co-ordinates of the point on the $\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{y}=6$ at which the tangent is equally inclined to the axes is
questions.explanation: Differentiating, y'=-\sqrt{y}/\sqrt{x}. Equally inclined means slope magnitude 1, so x=y; then $2\sqrt{x}=6\Rightarrow x=y=9$.

questions.q: The function f(x) = 4 sin$^3$x - 6 sin$^2$x + 12 sin x + 100 is strictly
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=12\cos x(\sin^2x-\sin x+1)$; the quadratic factor is always positive, so the sign of f'(x) equals the sign of $\cos x$, which is negative on $(\pi/2,\pi)$, making f strictly decreasing there.

questions.q: Area of the region bounded by the curve y = tan x, the x-axis and the line x = $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ is
questions.explanation: Area = \int_0^{\pi/3}\tan x\,dx = [-\ln\cos x]_0^{\pi/3} = -\ln(1/2) = \ln 2.

questions.q: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_2^3 x^2\,dx$ as the limit of a sum
$\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\cos x\sin x}{1+\sin x}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Put u=\sin x: \int_0^1\frac{u}{1+u}du = \int_0^1\left(1-\frac{1}{1+u}\right)du = 1-\ln 2.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\cos 2x - \cos 2\alpha}{\cos x - \cos \alpha}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Using sum-to-product identities the integrand simplifies to $2\cos x + 2\cos\alpha$, which integrates to $2(\sin x + x\cos\alpha)+c$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^1 \dfrac{xe^x}{(2+x)^3}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Since $\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{e^x}{(x+2)^2}\right] = \frac{xe^x}{(x+2)^3}$, the definite integral equals $\left[\frac{e^x}{(x+2)^2}\right]_0^1 = \frac{e}{9}-\frac{1}{4}$.

questions.q: If $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{(x+2)(x^2+1)} = a\log|1+x^2| + b\tan^{-1}x + \dfrac{1}{5}\log|x+2| + c$, then
questions.explanation: Partial fractions give $\frac{1}{5(x+2)} - \frac{x}{5(x^2+1)} + \frac{2}{5(x^2+1)}$, integrating to $\frac{1}{5}\ln|x+2| - \frac{1}{10}\ln(x^2+1) + \frac{2}{5}\tan^{-1}x + c$, so $a=-1/10, b=2/5$.

questions.q: If $|\vec a| = 2$ and $|\vec b| = 3$ and the angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ is 120°, then the length of the vector $\left|\dfrac{1}{2}\vec a - \dfrac{1}{3}\vec b\right|^2$ is
questions.explanation: $\left|\frac12\vec a-\frac13\vec b\right|^2=\frac14|\vec a|^2+\frac19|\vec b|^2-\frac13(\vec a\cdot\vec b)=1+1-\frac13(-3)=3$. Note: the KEA key marks this question as "1234" (all four options awarded), i.e. full marks given to everyone, even though only option C (3) is mathematically correct.

questions.q: If $|\vec a \times \vec b|^2 + |\vec a \cdot \vec b|^2 = 36$ and $|\vec a| = 3$ then $|\vec b|$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Using $|\vec a\times\vec b|^2+(\vec a\cdot\vec b)^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2$, we get $9|\vec b|^2=36\Rightarrow|\vec b|=2$. The printed question shows $|\vec a\times\vec b|$ without a square, which makes it dimensionally inconsistent (unanswerable as literally printed) — the KEA key awarded a grace mark for this question, most likely because of this printing error. (as per KEA key)

questions.q: If $\vec\alpha = \hat i - 3\hat j$, $\vec\beta = \hat i + 2\hat j - \hat k$ then express $\vec\beta$ in the form $\vec\beta = \vec\beta_1 + \vec\beta_2$ where $\vec\beta_1$ is parallel to $\vec\alpha$ and $\vec\beta_2$ is perpendicular to $\vec\alpha$ then $\vec\beta_1$ is given by
questions.explanation: $\vec\beta_1=\frac{\vec\alpha\cdot\vec\beta}{|\vec\alpha|^2}\vec\alpha=\frac{-5}{10}(\hat i-3\hat j)=-\frac12(\hat i-3\hat j)$, which does not match any printed option exactly — this appears to be a defective question, consistent with the KEA key awarding a grace mark here. Option (A) is picked as the closest in form. (as per KEA key)

questions.q: The sum of the degree and order of the differential equation $(1+y_1^2)^{2/3} = y_2$ is
questions.explanation: Cubing both sides gives $(1+y_1^2)^2=y_2^3$, a polynomial equation of degree 3 in the highest derivative $y_2$ (order 2). Sum = 2+3 = 5.

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = x^2$, then 2y(2) - y(1) =
questions.explanation: IF = x, giving $xy=\frac{x^4}{4}+C$, so $y=\frac{x^3}{4}+\frac{C}{x}$. Then $2y(2)-y(1)=2\left(2+\frac C2\right)-\left(\frac14+C\right)=4-\frac14=\frac{15}{4}$ (C cancels).

questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (x+y)^2$ is
questions.explanation: Put $v=x+y$: $\frac{dv}{dx}=1+v^2$, so $\tan^{-1}v = x+c$, i.e. $\tan^{-1}(x+y)=x+c$.

questions.q: If y(x) be the solution of differential equation $x\log x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 2x\log x$, y(e) is equal to
questions.explanation: The general solution is $y\ln x = 2x\ln x - 2x + C$. Requiring y to stay finite (regular) as $x\to1$ (where $\ln x\to0$) forces $C=2$, giving $y(e)=2e-2e+2=2$. The question's answer is genuinely ambiguous without this extra regularity condition (no initial value is explicitly given), which is likely why KEA awarded a grace mark. (as per KEA key)

questions.q: A dietician has to develop a special diet using two foods X and Y. Each packet (containing 30 g) of food X contains 12 units of calcium, 4 units of iron, 6 units of cholesterol and 6 units of vitamin A. Each packet of the same quantity of food Y contains 3 units of calcium, 20 units of iron, 4 units of cholesterol and 3 units of vitamin A. The diet requires atleast 240 units of calcium, atleast 460 units of iron and atmost 300 units of cholesterol. The corner points of the feasible region are
questions.explanation: Solving the calcium, iron and cholesterol constraints pairwise gives the feasible region's corner points as (2, 72), (40, 15) and (15, 20), the standard result for this diet LPP.

The co-ordinates of foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the plane 2x - 3y + 4z = 29 are
questions.explanation: Foot $=\left(\frac{2d}{29},\frac{-3d}{29},\frac{4d}{29}\right)$ with $d=29$, giving (2, -3, 4).

questions.q: The angle between the pair of lines $\dfrac{x+3}{3}=\dfrac{y-1}{5}=\dfrac{z+3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{1}=\dfrac{y-4}{4}=\dfrac{z-5}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: Using direction ratios (3,5,4) and (1,4,2), $\cos\theta=\dfrac{31}{5\sqrt{42}}\approx0.957$, which does not match any of the printed options exactly — this appears to be a defective question (matching numbers do not exist among the choices), consistent with the KEA grace mark. Option (C) is closest numerically. (as per KEA key)

questions.q: The corner points of the feasible region of an LPP are (0, 2), (3, 0), (6, 0), (6, 8) and (0, 5) then the minimum value of z = 4x + 6y occurs at
questions.explanation: z equals 12 at both (0,2) and (3,0); since the minimum value is attained at two adjacent corner points, it is attained at every point on the segment joining them — infinite number of points.

questions.q: If A and B are two independent events such that P($\bar A$) = 0.75, P(A ∪ B) = 0.65, and P(B) = x, then find the value of x:
questions.explanation: P(A)=0.25. For independent events, $0.25+x-0.25x=0.65\Rightarrow0.75x=0.4\Rightarrow x=\frac{8}{15}$.

questions.q: Find the mean number of heads in three tosses of a fair coin:
questions.explanation: Mean = np = 3 \times \frac12 = 1.5.

The probabilities are 0.7 that there will be a lockdown, 0.8 that the pandemic is controlled in one month if there is a lockdown and 0.3 that it is controlled in one month if there is no lockdown. The probability that the pandemic will be controlled in one month is
questions.explanation: By total probability: $0.7\times0.8+0.3\times0.3=0.56+0.09=0.65$.

questions.explanation: Using $2+2\cos X=4\cos^2(X/2)$ repeatedly (with X=8\theta, then 4\theta, then 2\theta) reduces the nested radical to $2\cos\theta$.

questions.q: If A = {1, 2, 3, ...... 10} then number of subsets of A containing only odd numbers is
questions.explanation: The odd numbers {1,3,5,7,9} form a 5-element set, which has $2^5=32$ subsets; excluding the empty subset gives 31 non-empty subsets containing only odd numbers.

questions.q: Suppose that the number of elements in set A is p, the number of elements in set B is q and the number of elements in A×B is 7 then p$^2$ + q$^2$ =
questions.explanation: Since $pq=7$ (7 prime), $(p,q)=(1,7)$ or $(7,1)$, giving $p^2+q^2=1+49=50$ in either case.

questions.q: The domain of the function f(x) = $\dfrac{1}{\log_{10}(1-x)} + \sqrt{x+2}$ is
questions.explanation: Need $x\ge-2$, $1-x>0\Rightarrow x<1$, and $\log_{10}(1-x)\ne0\Rightarrow x\ne0$, giving $[-2,0)\cup(0,1)$.

questions.q: The trigonometric function y = tan x in the II quadrant
questions.explanation: For $x\in(\pi/2,\pi)$, tan x rises from $-\infty$ (just past $\pi/2$) to 0 (at $\pi$), i.e. it increases from $-\infty$ to 0.

questions.q: The octant in which the point (2, -4, -7) lies is
questions.explanation: Signs (+, -, -) correspond to the eighth octant.

questions.q: If f(x) = $\begin{cases}x^2-1, & 0<x<2\\ 2x+3, & 2\le x<3\end{cases}$, the quadratic equation whose roots are $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to2^-}f(x)$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to2^+}f(x)$ is
questions.explanation: $\lim_{x\to2^-}f(x)=4-1=3$ and $\lim_{x\to2^+}f(x)=4+3=7$. Equation with roots 3, 7: $x^2-10x+21=0$.

questions.q: If 3x + i(4x - y) = 6 - i where x and y are real numbers, then the values of x and y are respectively,
questions.explanation: Equating real parts: $3x=6\Rightarrow x=2$. Equating imaginary parts: $4x-y=-1\Rightarrow y=9$.

questions.q: If all permutations of the letters of the word MASK are arranged in the order as in dictionary with or without meaning, which one of the following is 19$^{th}$ word?
questions.explanation: Alphabetical letters A, K, M, S each start 6 words (3! each): words 1-6 start with A, 7-12 with K, 13-18 with M, 19-24 with S. The 19th word is the first S-word, formed as S followed by A,K,M in order, i.e. SAKM — which is not among the printed options, so this appears to be a defective question, consistent with the KEA grace mark. Option (C) is picked as the closest. (as per KEA key)

If the straight line 2x - 3y + 17 = 0 is perpendicular to the line passing through the points (7, 17) and (15, β), then β equals
questions.explanation: The given line has slope $2/3$, so the perpendicular slope is $-3/2$. $\frac{\beta-17}{15-7}=-\frac32\Rightarrow\beta=17-12=5$.

$\displaystyle\lim_{y\to0}\dfrac{\sqrt{3+y^3}-\sqrt3}{y^3}$ =
questions.explanation: With $t=y^3\to0$, the limit is the derivative of $\sqrt{3+t}$ at $t=0$, which is $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt3}$.

questions.q: If the standard deviation of the numbers -1, 0, 1, k is $\sqrt5$ where k > 0, then k is equal to
questions.explanation: Mean $=k/4$. Setting variance $=\frac{2+k^2}{4}-\frac{k^2}{16}=5$ gives $8+3k^2=80\Rightarrow k^2=24\Rightarrow k=2\sqrt6$.

questions.q: If the set x contains 7 elements and set y contains 8 elements, then the number of bijections from x to y is
questions.explanation: A bijection requires equal cardinalities; since $7\ne8$, there are no bijections.

If A = $\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1\\0 & 0\end{bmatrix}$ then (aI + bA)$^n$ is (where I is the identity matrix of order 2)
questions.explanation: Since $A^2=0$, the binomial expansion of $(aI+bA)^n$ truncates after the linear term: $a^nI + na^{n-1}bA$.

questions.q: If A is a 3×3 matrix such that |5·adj A| = 5 then |A| is equal to
questions.explanation: $|5\,\text{adj}A|=5^3|\text{adj}A|=125|A|^2=5\Rightarrow|A|^2=\frac{1}{25}\Rightarrow|A|=\pm\frac15$.

questions.q: If there are two values of 'a' which makes determinant $\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 & 5\\2 & a & -1\\0 & 4 & 2a\end{vmatrix}=86$ Then the sum of these numbers is
questions.explanation: Expanding, $2a^2+8a+44=86\Rightarrow a^2+4a-21=0\Rightarrow(a+7)(a-3)=0$, so $a=-7,3$ and their sum is $-4$.

questions.q: If A is a matrix of order 3 × 3, then (A$^2$)$^{-1}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $(A^2)^{-1} = (A^{-1})^2$ by the standard inverse-of-a-power identity.

questions.q: If A = $\begin{bmatrix}2 & -1\\3 & -2\end{bmatrix}$, then the inverse of the matrix A$^3$ is
questions.explanation: Direct computation gives $A^2=I$, so $A^3=A$, and hence $(A^3)^{-1}=A^{-1}=A$ (since here $A^{-1}=A$).

questions.q: If A is a skew symmetric matrix, then A$^{2021}$ is
questions.explanation: For skew symmetric A ($A^T=-A$), odd powers satisfy $(A^n)^T=(-A)^n=-A^n$ for odd n, so $A^{2021}$ is also skew symmetric.
